description: Our interests include astrophysics, cosmology, programming, and scientific research. We have experience with Python, data analysis, STEAM projects, and science communication. We enjoy combining astronomy and technology to solve problems, and we are excited to collaborate with creative people from different backgrounds to build innovative solutions.
summary:
PROJECT JEZERO: ODYSSEY I is an interactive survival and exploration guide designed to support future human missions to Mars, specifically in Jezero Crater. Our project combines scientific research, technology, programming, and interactive mapping to create a tool for exploring the Red Planet.

We developed a 3D map of Mars, an interactive interface, and a scientific exploration route connecting six points of interest, beginning and ending at a proposed base. Using data from NASA missions, particularly the Perseverance rover, we selected locations with important geological features and scientific value.

Our project addresses the challenge of Mars exploration by providing a guide that helps astronauts navigate previously studied areas, plan scientific investigations, access relevant information, and identify routes back to their starting point. This is important because it demonstrates how interactive technology and scientific data can contribute to safer and more organized exploration.

Ultimately, PROJECT JEZERO: ODYSSEY I aims to contribute to our understanding of Mars and take a small step toward making future human exploration and habitation beyond Earth possible.
details: Project Jezero: Odyssey I is a Mars exploration project designed to support future astronauts during human missions to the Red Planet. Its main component, ARES, is an interactive 3D mapping system that allows users to explore Mars, zoom into Jezero Crater, visualize different scientific layers, identify important locations, and plan potential exploration routes. The platform integrates information about topography, temperature, geology, minerals, and environmental conditions to help astronauts understand the terrain, identify scientific opportunities, and make safer decisions. We developed the project using technologies such as React, TypeScript, Three.js, and geospatial tools, incorporating scientific data from NASA and other reliable sources. What makes our project creative is the integration of different types of planetary data into one interactive environment instead of presenting them as separate maps or documents. During development, our team considered astronaut safety, scientific value, terrain conditions, navigation, data reliability, and usability. Our ultimate goal is to demonstrate how an integrated digital mapping system could make future human exploration of Mars more informed, efficient, and safe.
